connections.why: Enzymes are globular proteins, so protein structure determines how they catalyse reactions
Transcription and translation of DNA build the polypeptides that fold into proteins
Phospholipids form the bilayer of the fluid mosaic membrane that controls transport
Glucose from carbohydrates is the hexose substrate that glycolysis breaks down
Knowing DNA structure makes producing recombinant DNA possible
Specialised cells form the exchange surfaces of insects, fish, mammals and plants
Crossing over and independent assortment in meiosis are key sources of variation
A small SA:V ratio in large organisms drives the need for a mass transport system
Selective reabsorption in the kidney relies on active transport across membranes
Haemoglobin in the blood the heart pumps carries oxygen to respiring tissues
Hydrostatic pressure from circulation forces tissue fluid out of capillaries
The autonomic nervous system adjusts the cardiac cycle of the heart
Photosynthesis stores the energy that respiration releases as ATP
When oxygen is absent, glycolysis continues but pyruvate becomes lactate or ethanol
Understanding prokaryotic cells underpins how bacteria are cultured and counted
The humoral and cell-mediated responses defend against invading bacterial pathogens
Overuse of bactericidal and bacteriostatic antibiotics selects for resistant strains
Resistance spreads as natural selection favours bacteria that survive antibiotics
Mutation and meiosis supply the variation that natural selection acts upon
Evolutionary relationships from natural selection underpin how organisms are classified
Inheritance of alleles determines the allele frequencies that selection changes
Sequencing reveals the genes whose expression transcription factors regulate
Drugs act by altering the synaptic transmission described in nervous transmission
The nervous system and hypothalamus drive much homeostatic regulation
Photosynthesis fixes the energy that then flows between trophic levels
Human activity and conservation treaties like CITES shape global biodiversity
Sampling and trophic structure reveal how communities develop through succession
